title: OAuth 2.0 / OIDC vs SAML
description: Comparing token-based delegated authorization and OpenID Connect with XML-based enterprise federation.
question: Should our login and federation use OIDC/OAuth or SAML?

sections.overview: OAuth 2.0 is an authorization framework for delegated access with tokens; OpenID Connect adds an identity layer for login. SAML 2.0 is an XML-based standard for browser single sign-on, common in enterprise identity providers.
whenToUse: OIDC/OAuth: new applications, mobile and SPA clients, API access tokens.
SAML: enterprise customers whose identity providers require it.
whenNotToUse: SAML for API authorization or mobile apps.
Rolling your own token handling instead of a vetted library or provider.
sections.summary: Build on OIDC; add SAML when enterprise customers ask for it.

values: Strong when following current best practices (PKCE, short-lived tokens)
Mature; XML signature handling is error-prone

relations.note: Protocol choice leads to who implements it.

title: Managed Identity vs Custom Identity
description: Whether to use an identity provider service or build authentication and user management in-house.
question: Should we build our own authentication or use an identity provider?

sections.overview: Managed identity providers handle sign-up, login, MFA, password storage, federation and token issuance. Custom identity means your team implements and secures these.
whenToUse: Managed: almost always, especially for small teams and products needing SSO and MFA.
Custom: unusual requirements a provider cannot meet, or very large scale where cost dominates and a dedicated identity team exists.
whenNotToUse: Managed identity when its pricing per active user breaks unit economics at your scale (re-evaluate periodically).
failureModes: Weak password hashing or session handling in custom systems.
Credentials and signing keys scattered across services (secret sprawl).
Provider outage locking all users out.
sections.summary: Buy identity unless you can staff a team to own it.

values: Specialist-run; MFA and threat detection built in

relations.note: A specific build vs buy decision.
Custom auth spreads signing keys and credentials.
Identity is the foundation of zero trust.

title: Zero Trust
description: A security model that authenticates and authorizes every request regardless of network location.

sections.overview: Zero trust removes implicit trust based on network location. Every access decision uses identity, device posture and policy, and connections are encrypted.
application: User access: identity-aware proxies instead of VPN-wide access.
sections.limitations: Zero trust is a direction, not a product. Partial adoption with a flat internal network still leaves lateral movement open.
sections.summary: Assume the network is hostile; authenticate and authorize every request.

relations.note: Workload identity reduces reliance on static shared secrets.

title: Secrets Management
description: Storing, distributing, rotating and auditing credentials through a central system instead of code and config files.

sections.overview: A secrets manager stores credentials encrypted, controls access by identity, issues short-lived or rotated secrets, and records who accessed what.
whenNotToUse: Do not put secrets in code, images, CI logs or plain environment files committed to repositories.
implementation: Prefer workload identity and short-lived credentials.
Scan repositories and images for leaked secrets.
failureModes: The secrets manager as a single point of failure at startup.
sections.summary: Centralize secrets, shorten their lifetime, and audit access.

title: HashiCorp Vault
description: A secrets management system offering dynamic secrets, encryption as a service and identity-based access.

sections.overview: Vault stores and issues secrets, generates short-lived database and cloud credentials, runs a PKI and provides encryption APIs, with detailed audit logs.
whenNotToUse: Running Vault highly available is itself operational work; cloud-native managers may suffice on one cloud.
sections.summary: Powerful secrets platform; budget for operating it.
